papers.title: A Hybrid State Space-Attention Architecture for Forecasting the Trajectories of Battery Degradation
papers.abstract: Early-life battery degradation trajectory forecasting aims to predict a battery cell's full state-of-health (SOH) trajectory from its initial charge-discharge cycles, potentially reducing cell qualification and evaluation time from months to days. Despite recent advances, accurate forecasting remains challenging for emerging battery chemistries, data-scarce domains, and cells exhibiting degradation behaviors beyond those observed during training. Existing state-of-the-art approaches increasingly rely on model scaling, large language model-derived aging-condition embeddings, and extensive fold-specific hyperparameter tuning, raising concerns about computational efficiency, reproducibility, and generalization. This work introduces DecayFormer, a compact hybrid state-space and attention architecture designed for early-life degradation trajectory forecasting. DecayFormer combines cycle-level selective recurrence, using a single scalar state per channel, with an attention mechanism queried by the recurrent state. It further incorporates state-of-charge (SOC) interval statistics and a master curve head that jointly estimates a scalar lifetime and a monotonically non-increasing SOH profile parameterized by normalized lifetime. We evaluate DecayFormer on the BatteryLife benchmark using all 22 aging-condition-exclusive folds, with a single run per fold and one fixed configuration across all folds, without fold-specific tuning. DecayFormer achieves mean test MAPE values of 2.25% on Li-ion, 2.76% on CALB, 0.95% on Na-ion, and 7.19% on Zn-ion. These results demonstrate the potential of compact sequence models to deliver accurate early-life degradation forecasts across diverse battery chemistries and aging conditions, without relying on extensive model scaling or per-fold optimization.

papers.title: Vibe synthesis: hierarchical agentic decision-making for intent-driven multistep molecule synthesis
papers.abstract: The ability to construct complex molecules underpins advances in medicine and the molecular sciences. Yet long-horizon multistep synthesis requires decisions to be revised as evidence accumulates across chemically dependent operations, a capability not readily supported by artificial-intelligence tools and automated platforms organized around predefined tasks and hard-coded workflows. Here we propose and demonstrate a vibe synthesis system (VibeSyn), an intent-driven architecture in which hierarchical agents translate chemist-defined molecular objectives and accumulating evidence into adaptive decisions executed through computational tools and laboratory automation. We evaluate VibeSyn in three demonstrations of increasing scope and autonomy, progressing from evidence-grounded experimental decisions to adaptive execution of a ten-step total synthesis of catharanthine and structure-to-compound synthesis of cyclic peptides containing unnatural amino acids (uAAs). Across the long-horizon campaigns, active human input and simple confirmation account for less than 7.5% and 5.2%, respectively, of recorded workflow actions and outcomes. VibeSyn points towards a future in which chemists define synthetic intent and agent-directed laboratories autonomously navigate the evolving experimental trajectory required to deliver the target compound.

papers.title: Nahual: A Sequence Model for Language and Atoms
papers.abstract: Generative models play a rapidly growing role in the design and simulation of molecules. The most widely used applications of generative models are in large language models (LLMs), owing to the natural flexibility of language for specifying and answering queries. However, generalist LLMs do not effectively handle large sets of 3D coordinates, whereas specialist generative models of 3D molecules cannot reach the controllability afforded by language. To bridge these capabilities, we propose Nahual, a decoder-only autoregressive diffusion model for any sequence of text and 3D molecules. To enable expressive autoregression on continuous coordinates, we propose next-token diffusion, whereby a causal transformer denoises each token while attending to the clean tokens before it, without increasing context size. We train Nahual on a curated set of twelve 3D chemistry tasks ranging from microsolvation to molecular conformer search to adsorption on metal surfaces, with associated evaluation metrics and baselines. The result is a single set of end-to-end-trained weights that simultaneously performs all tasks and surpasses state-of-the-art models specialized for crystal structure prediction and property-conditional molecule generation. Our results demonstrate the viability of scaling generalist decoder-only models for native multimodal understanding and generation across language and chemistry. Code is available at https://github.com/the-matter-lab/nahual.

papers.title: MolReps: Taking SELFIES, Making SMILES, Teaching LLMs
papers.abstract: The same molecule can be expressed in multiple, syntactically distinct representations, yet it remains unclear whether large language models (LLMs) can recognize and relate these equivalent encodings. We introduce MolReps, a pipeline that generates 9,600 question-answer pairs across ten representations for conversion, normalization, and 2D structure recognition. Post-training on MolReps improves text-only and multimodal models, MolQwen3-4B-Instruct (MQ3-4B-I) and MolQwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (MQ3-VL-4B-I), from $4.01\%$ to $75.13\%$ and from $7.11\%$ to $73.14\%$ (InChIKey match) on the molecule-overlap test set, respectively. On the molecule-disjoint test set, post-training increased validity from $20.35\%$ to $58.12\%$ for MQ3-4B-I and from $17.19\%$ to $59.34\%$ for MQ3-VL-4B-I. However, InChIKey match remained low, decreasing from $3.86\%$ to $3.09\%$ and from $6.44\%$ to $2.29\%$, respectively. Furthermore, the resulting models achieve a relative $27.84\%$ improvement in average over their base model on MolRepBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating molecular property prediction. These results show the effectiveness of targeted post-training for enhancing molecular representation understanding and its potential to improve downstream molecular tasks.

papers.title: Rotation-Invariant Machine Learning for Highly Symmetric Molecular Configurations
papers.abstract: Atomistic machine learning can approximate expensive quantum mechanical calculations at a fraction of their computational cost, but accuracy depends strongly on how the three-dimensional atomic environments are represented. Invariant representations enable fast computation but can fail to distinguish geometrically distinct configurations, especially in highly symmetric environments. We introduce a lightweight benchmark to evaluate expressivity on $n$-fold symmetric configurations, and use it to expose degeneracies in both invariant and equivariant architectures. Guided by these results, we construct a new invariant basis for HIP-HOP which resolves most of the identified failures. On a methane simulation dataset, the extended basis achieves the lowest error among the HIP-HOP variants and has similar accuracy to EquiformerV3 while running $3.2\times$ faster at inference. These results show that carefully constructed invariant representations can mitigate key expressivity limitations while balancing accuracy and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Application-Oriented Evaluation of CPU/GPU Quantum Simulators: From Foundational Circuits to Quantum Chemistry
papers.abstract: Quantum computing simulators underpin the development and prototyping of quantum algorithms, yet the practical choice between competing software stacks and their CPU and GPU backends is rarely guided by application-oriented evidence. We present a systematic, quantum hardware-agnostic evaluation of two widely used stacks, CUDA-Q and Qiskit, selected as the simulators closest to production execution paths, across CPU and GPU backends, and across single- and double-precision arithmetic. The evaluation spans foundational utility circuits (GHZ-state preparation and QFT/QFT$^\dagger$ mirror circuits) through applied quantum chemistry (Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) energy estimation with standard UCCSD and a depth-reduced LCNot-UCCSD ansatz, and direct sampling on hydrogen chains up to 32 qubits). The results yield concrete selection guidance: GPU-accelerated double precision delivers consistent speedups, typically $2\times$ to $10\times$ for tractable application workloads and substantially larger at the widest circuits up to $100\times$ or more, and governs the maximum simulable system size under fixed compute memory, while CPU statevector backends and Qiskit Aer remain competitive, and at times preferable, at low qubit counts and wide but shallow circuits. We demonstrate the practical payoff of this guidance by extending an in-house developed QSCI(LCNot-UCCSD)-RBM electronic-structure workflow, previously constrained to a 16-qubit active space on a CPU, to a 32-qubit (10 electrons, 16 orbitals) active space with GPU acceleration, completing a 20-point potential-energy-surface scan of N$_{2}$ in the cc-pVDZ basis. This end-to-end evaluation establishes that the principled simulator selection translates directly into expanded scientific reach and faster algorithmic prototyping.

papers.title: Variational Monte Carlo for Quantum Excited States via Nested Low-Rank Approximation
papers.abstract: The electronic Schr\"odinger equation encodes a molecule's electronic structure and quantum properties, but solving it scales exponentially with the number of electrons. Solving this equation with neural-network variational Monte Carlo (VMC) has reached chemical accuracy on the ground state of small molecules; extending this success to excited states is constrained by two existing paradigms. Penalty-based methods need $K$ Laplacians per step but require tuning the overlap-penalty weights against the energy gaps they aim to compute. Natural excited states VMC (NES-VMC) is penalty-free, but it combines the $K$ ansatzes into one determinant, whose local energy requires $K^2$ Laplacians per step. We resolve this trade-off via low-rank approximation (LoRA) reparameterization of the rank-$K$ variational objective. The reparameterized objective admits a VMC-compatible stochastic gradient estimator via MCMC sampling from the per-state Born densities, and a sequential nesting scheme recovers the lowest $K$ eigenstates in eigenvalue order. The resulting algorithm, NestedLoRA-VMC, inherits a global optimality guarantee from the LoRA principle. On the first-row atoms Li through Ne at $K=10$, its accuracy is comparable to that of NES-VMC and of a state-of-the-art penalty-based method.

papers.title: Out-of-training properties in frozen interatomic potential embeddings are decodable and ordered by physical scale
papers.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are trained on energies, forces and stresses, yet their frozen representations can predict other materials properties. We probe ORB-v3 and UMA-S across layers, read-outs and equivariant channels for nine properties of 154,875 Materials Project crystals. Both models outperform composition-only descriptors on all targets, including five outside their training objectives; errors in physical units help assess potential screening applications. Optimal depth varies by property, consistent with a physical-scale ordering. Random-weight controls reveal strongly property-dependent benefits of pretraining. UMA-S's rotation-invariant angular channels improve crystal-system classification, while higher scores from its full tensor disappear under rotation; matched-model controls do not isolate equivariance as the explanation. Accuracy varies across different probes, but nearest-neighbour prediction often approaches XGBoost performance, even though materials do not form distinct clusters according to their properties. We also test whether a linear predictor trained on one model's embeddings can predict properties using the other model's embeddings after a learned linear transformation. Predictive accuracy is largely preserved, despite differences in which atoms the two models place close together. These results guide the reuse of frozen MLIP representations for materials prediction.

papers.title: Self-attention is a Dyson equation for many-body machine learning
papers.abstract: Why does symmetric sum-pooling (DeepSets) predict ground-state potentials to sub-meV accuracy, yet fail for correlated wavefunctions and excited states? Sum-pooling is a mean-field (Hartree) model: its $O(1/N)$ off-diagonal Jacobian suffices for nearsighted ground-state energies, but erases nonlocal two-body correlations. We show that self-attention is a real-space Dyson iteration whose Boltzmann (softmax) kernel acts as a two-body self-energy. Because physical Hamiltonians act pairwise, L\"owdin's 2-RDM theorem and the Galitskii--Migdal relation guarantee that iterating a two-body propagator captures the full energetics of correlated matter. When fitting a fractal backflow determinant, DeepSets blurs the nodal surface onto a mean-field envelope, whereas self-attention recovers the fractal attractor. Seen through this lens, the unreasonable effectiveness of attention is not an accident; in a universe built from pairwise interactions, two-body attention is all you need.

papers.title: Variational and geometric time-dependent density-functional theory of electronic systems
papers.abstract: A central problem in time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) is to construct a time-dependent many-electron wave function that reproduces a prescribed time-dependent electron density. This problem admits a natural geometric interpretation, which in turn leads to at least two distinct formulations of TDDFT. The first is the usual variational formulation of TDDFT, in which the density constraint is enforced with a real-valued local potential. The second is geometric TDDFT, introduced in recent works, in which the same density constraint is enforced with an imaginary local potential, or equivalently with a Hermitian nonlocal potential. In this work, we develop this unified viewpoint for continuous electronic systems and systematically compare the two formulations. We formulate the corresponding time-dependent Kohn-Sham schemes and derive a number of exact conditions for geometric TDDFT, including conditions associated with causality, time-reversal symmetry, uniform-coordinate scaling, translational invariance, energy and momentum equations of motion, one-electron self-interaction, and the adiabatic limit. The paper also contains a mathematical section where we provide a fully rigorous justification of some parts of the text. We particularly discuss the mathematical properties of two operators underlying the two formulations of TDDFT and establish sufficient conditions for their invertibility. We explain the functional-analytic subtleties underlying the geometric interpretation of TDDFT and the two formulations of TDDFT. This unified perspective clarifies the mathematical and conceptual relation between variational and geometric TDDFT and provides a foundation for the development of approximations within geometric TDDFT.

papers.title: Exploring Energy Landscapes for Functional Materials: Ga vacancies in $\beta$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$
papers.abstract: Energy landscape exploration requires extensive energy and force evaluations, making efficient access to interatomic potentials an important practical challenge. We present a persistent socket interface that connects the landscape exploration tools in the GMIN, OPTIM, and PATHSAMPLE programs to potentials available through the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE). The persistent design keeps both the calculator and socket connection active throughout the search, avoiding repeated initialisation. We apply this framework to understand and predict the properties of Ga vacancies in $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ using two NequIP-based potentials, and construct kinetic transition networks describing complex vacancy configurations and migration pathways. Temperature-dependent analysis of the dominant paths reveals how the most probable migration sequence can change, with the mechanism governed by global properties of the network, rather than simply the highest energy barrier. Visualisation, mean first-passage times, and heat capacities enable us to connect the organisation of the landscape to relaxation time scales and thermodynamic observables. The interface extends energy landscape methods to ASE-compatible atomistic models, providing a general framework for combining global optimisation, transition state searches, kinetic network analysis, and thermodynamic characterisation with recent developments in machine-learned interatomic potentials.

papers.title: A new chemical network to explore the disequilibrium chemistry of silicates and iron in hot gas giants
papers.abstract: Chemical equilibrium modeling of gas giant planet atmospheres has shown that the production and condensation of silicates plays an important role in shaping their final composition. However, no chemical kinetics network for these species are available, preventing the opportunity to analyze the impact of chemical disequilibrium processes. In this paper we present \texttt{SILANE}, a new chemical network that include Mg, Si, Fe and 15 carriers of these elements, including MgSiO$_3$ and Mg$_2$SiO$_4$, ready for use in the VULCAN code. We compare the results of our network with a chemical equilibrium model and discuss them in relation to previous results from literature. We then apply our new network to the analysis of a vertically mixed, Solar-composition atmosphere with equilibrium temperatures $T_{eq}$ in the [700, 1600] K range, finding that (i) rock-forming silicates disappears from the upper atmosphere already at 1100 K, (ii) SiH$_4$ reaches concentrations of $10^{-7}$ in the upper ($P\le 1.0$ bar) atmosphere for planets with $T_{eq}\in$ [800, 1100] K and (iii) the amount of oxygen in refractories decrease from 21\% at $T_{eq}$=700 K to essentially zero already at 1000 K, while in the classical equilibrium framework it remains constant up to $T_{eq}$=1300 K. By applying our network to the case of the young hot Jupiter YSES-1 c and comparing both the mixing ratios of volatile species and the enstatite fraction in the silicate mix, we find evidence of a well-mixed atmosphere, possibly with an average $K_{zz} \ge 10^{10}$ cm$^{2}$s$^{-1}$ up to the $10^{-4}$ bar level.

papers.title: Adsorbate-Free Screening of Dissociative Water Adsorption on Nickel Nanoparticles via Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Dissociative water adsorption is a key step in heterogeneous and electrochemical catalysis, but on finite Ni nanosystems the OH$^*$ and H$^*$ fragments can occupy many combinations of surface sites, making exhaustive density functional theory (DFT) screening impractical. We introduce a graph neural network (GNN) framework with an adsorbate-free representation: candidate O- and H-binding sites are defined by sets of Ni atoms (\textit{anchors}), and each site pair is encoded as a graph constructed solely from these anchors and their local Ni environment. Using only MACE-relaxed bare Ni geometries as input, separate GNNs predict the DFT-reference adsorption energies of OH$^*$+H$^*$ configurations and whether the proposed binding sites would be retained upon DFT relaxation, eliminating the need to construct or relax adsorbates during screening. Trained across Ni nanoclusters and Ni(111)/Ni(100) surfaces, the energy model achieves a mean absolute error of 0.031 eV on the internal validation set and demonstrates transferability to unseen Ni$_{55}$, Ni$_{91}$, and Ni$_{130}$ clusters and larger surface cells, particularly for relative-energy ranking, although quantitative accuracy varies across systems. These independent tests also support the retention classifier's use as a conservative filter for selecting configurations likely to preserve their proposed binding sites. Application to Ni nanoparticles containing up to $\sim$3000 atoms identifies favorable co-adsorption motifs and shows that lower O-site coordination generally stabilizes the dissociated state, whereas H-site coordination has a weaker influence. The framework thus offers an efficient route to screening adsorption energetics, with potential extensions to other metals and adsorbate combinations.

papers.title: Bias Conditioning and Long-Range Electrostatics for Consistent Machine-Learning Potentials of Electrified Interfaces
papers.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) of electrified interfaces need the bias as input, but it is unclear whether a scalar electrode charge suffices and whether short-range models capture the non-local response. We add charge and field conditioning to short- and long-range MLIPs. State-of-the-art field-conditioned short-range models overpolarize thick water films nearly twofold and miss work-function shifts at stepped Pt. Our long-range model captures both, needs only the electrode charge at metals as input, and reproduces ab initio simulations of the Pt(111)--water interface.

papers.title: Dissipative many-body theory of electron-phonon-photon systems
papers.abstract: Optical cavities offer opportunities to control quantum materials, but radiative leakage and vibrational relaxation call for microscopic theories that treat interactions and dissipation on equal footing. We develop a Keldysh-Lindblad nonequilibrium Green's function framework for interacting electrons coupled to quantized photon and phonon fields. The formulation accommodates boson-number-nonconserving Hamiltonians and dissipative channels that combine electronic transitions with bosonic processes. We derive the mixed electron-boson diagrammatic expansion and the corresponding Kadanoff-Baym equations, retaining environmental noise, initial correlations, and interaction-induced memory. The equal-time equations govern the electronic density matrix and the bosonic covariance. As an illustration, we construct jump operators that preserve a semiconductor with filled valence bands and an empty photon field. Within a mean-field treatment, this state remains stationary although its two-time propagators exhibit dissipative broadening. The framework opens new avenues for studying correlated dynamics in lossy cavities and vibrational environments.

papers.title: Real-time dynamics with bead-Fourier path integrals. III. Atomistic condensed-phase simulations
papers.abstract: Accurately accounting for nuclear quantum effects (NQEs), including zero-point energy and nuclear tunneling, is essential for a reliable prediction of the structural, thermodynamic, and dynamical properties of chemical systems, particularly those involving light atoms. However, incorporating NQEs could render simulations of large-scale chemical systems computationally prohibitive, particularly when combined with expensive electronic-structure calculations. One potential avenue for reducing cost is to use bead-Fourier path integrals (BF-PIs). In Paper I, we introduced the BF centroid molecular dynamics (BF-CMD) method, in which BF-PIs were used to compute an effective potential for CMD, and in Paper II, we introduced BF ring polymer MD (BF-RPMD), taking the BF-PI and using it for approximate real-time dynamics. Both papers featured a series of model systems and were able to reduce the number of beads needed to converge dynamical properties by a factor of 2 to 4, depending on the system. In this work, we report the first implementation and application of the BF-PI framework to atomistic simulations using liquid bulk water and hexagonal ice as test cases. As in our previous papers, we find that adding just a single Fourier component to the path yields a 4- and 8-fold reduction in the number of beads while achieving results that agree with reference PI simulations for liquid water and ice, respectively. We also demonstrate that we can reduce simulation costs by up to 5.5x compared to standard PIs by reducing the number of force calculations and normal-mode transformations.

papers.title: Hydration-induced local diffusivity heterogeneity modulates aqueous $H_2+OH$ reaction kinetics
papers.abstract: At room temperature, a Kramers reaction rate calculated with homogeneous solvent friction exceeds the measured rate of the aqueous reaction $H_2 + OH -> H + H_2O$ by about an order of magnitude. We show that spatially correlated hydration-induced diffusivity fluctuations increase effective friction and suppress the predicted escape rate. Estimates based on hydration-shell properties bring the theoretical rate closer to experiment. The suppression weakens with increasing temperature, linking local solvent heterogeneity to activated aqueous reaction kinetics.

papers.title: Formulation of Brownian chain molecular dynamics and the path-resolved quasi-density operator
papers.abstract: Brownian chain molecular dynamics (BCMD) [M. Shiga, J. Comput. Chem. 43, 1864 (2022)] was introduced as a practical path-integral-based approach to approximate quantum vibrational dynamics in molecular and condensed-phase systems. Its equations of motion combine Newtonian dynamics of the centroid variables with overdamped Brownian dynamics of the non-centroid path variables. Here, we introduce a path-resolved quasi-density-operator (path-QDO) representation by extending the QDO construction underlying centroid molecular dynamics to the full discretized imaginary-time path. For two position-diagonal observables, this representation gives an exact expression for the Kubo-transformed correlation function in the fine-discretization limit, without requiring either observable to be linear. BCMD can be viewed as a phenomenological, time-homogeneous Markov approximation to the exact reduced propagation in these path variables, although its generator is not derived from the path-QDO formulation. We also formulate and validate a multiple-time-step algorithm that allows pseudo-Hamiltonian errors in the deterministic propagation to be controlled by separating the Brownian refresh interval from the inner integration time step. We test the path-QDO representation on one-dimensional models and present BCMD infrared spectra of q-TIP4P/F ice, ambient water, and hot water, comparing them with published results from other approximate quantum-dynamics methods.

papers.title: Self-assembly of dipolar nanoclusters on an attractive substrate: A coarse-grained simulation approach
papers.abstract: Recently, Thomas et al. [Nanoscale 17, 18291 (2025)] showed that bismuth oxido nanoclusters (BiO-NCs) of the type [Bi$_{38}$ O$_{45}$ (Boc-L-Phe-O)$_{24}$] form chains when deposited onto gold or pyrolitic graphite substrates. This chain formation is significantly enhanced when the bismuth in the BiO-NCs is partially replaced by cerium through doping. In this work, we study a simplified, coarse-grained model of this process, namely (magnetic) Stockmayer particles in the presence of an attractive substrate. The model is investigated by means of molecular dynamics simulations. The deposition experiment is mimicked by a rapid quench from high temperature to a low temperature below the bulk coexistence curve. The results are found to be qualitatively similar to the experimental observations reported earlier. In our simulations, we find significant chain formation in the bulk even at rather low concentrations, which is in contrast to the BiO-NCs in ethanol for which dynamic light scattering reveals negligible aggregation in the absence of the substrate. This lends support to a scenario, conjectured in the work of Thomas at al., where the dipole moments are induced by the particle-substrate interaction and hence there is little dipole moment in the bulk. In a second part, we study the system in equilibrium. We consider the scaling of chains, the number of layers populated as a function of two-dimensional density, and we draw analogies to polymers on interfaces, which have been extensively studied over the past decades. Most notably, it is found that the chains behave as self-avoiding walks at low densities, which gives way to rod-like scaling at higher densities.

papers.title: GPRidge: Gaussian-process Accelerated Calculations of Minimum Energy Paths and First-order Saddle Points
authors: Andreas Lynge Vishart (Department of Energy Conversion and Storage
Thomas Bligaard (Department of Energy Conversion and Storage
papers.abstract: GPRidge, a Gaussian-process (GP) library for accelerating calculations of minimum energy paths and first-order saddle points with compiled-language and Python bindings, is presented. An evaluation controller uses GP predictions to iteratively adjust the Cartesian coordinates of the atoms. The fitted GP energy surface and measured energies and forces pass from the path calculation to local refinement of the saddle point. New evaluations improve the surrogate and check the candidate geometry. For the molecular calculations, acceptance requires measured-force convergence and an independent Hessian with only one negative eigenvalue. A second negative eigenvalue triggers an escape and renewed refinement. The controller supports a joint inverse-distance GP for molecules and local GP residuals on periodic systems. Applications to the 24 Baker-Chan and 20 Birkholz-Schlegel molecular reactions using the Universal Model for Atoms (UMA-S-1.1), and to 72 Pt heptamer and island rearrangements on Pt(111) using a Morse potential, are presented. On matched Baker-Chan reactions, GPRidge uses 7.8- and 7.0-fold fewer energy-and-force evaluations than climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) and off-path climbing-image nudged elastic band (OCI-NEB), respectively, reducing validation-inclusive CI-NEB time by 41%. All 20 Birkholz-Schlegel saddle points pass the independent index-one check, compared with 17 for the classical dimer method started from the same path maxima; on those 17 reactions, the GP dimer stage uses 6.4-fold fewer evaluations. All 72 Pt(111) paths meet the OptBench force criterion, with median evaluation counts of 30 and 23 for the heptamer and island problems, against 778 and 443 for CI-NEB.

papers.title: Solubility and Diffusion of Hydrogen Isotopes and Helium in Molten FLiBe
papers.abstract: Tritium produced in molten 2LiF-BeF$_2$ (FLiBe) may dissolve as T$_2$ or as TF, which differ greatly in solubility. Permeation experiments give a solubility close to that of HF and a flux proportional to the square root of the T$_2$ pressure, which has usually been taken as evidence of dissociation. We have developed a fixed-charge classical potential for FLiBe containing atomic tritium, T$_2$, TF, the hydride ion T$^-$ and helium, fitted only to periodic DFT calculations for hydrogen. The nuclei are classical, so the solubilities apply to all hydrogen isotopes. The host reproduces the measured density and neutron structure factor but is too fluid close to the liquidus. The calculated solubilities of T$_2$ and TF agree with experiment, and neither molecule dissociates in the melt. Because TF is much more soluble, it holds most of the dissolved tritium unless the salt is strongly reducing, and at constant redox potential its concentration varies with the square root of the T$_2$ pressure, which accounts for the permeation results without dissociation. Helium does not change the solubility of T$_2$: a helium bubble in the melt takes up T$_2$ as its Henry constant predicts, while TF is enriched at the bubble surface. T$_2$ diffuses somewhat faster than measured, and TF and T$^-$ two to three times more slowly than T$_2$.

papers.title: Liquid-liquid criticality in a fluid whose two structures favor mixing
papers.abstract: The generic two-state description of liquid polyamorphism requires a non-ideality opposing mixing for liquid-liquid separation. This condition assumes that the free energy of the underlying fluid is independent of the structural order, an assumption that fails when the local structures differ in size or attraction. We derive a closed-form stability condition after density relaxation for a van der Waals closure based on the second virial coefficient of a pair potential whose internal state determines both the contact distance and the well depth. The condition recovers the familiar result for structures identical in size and attraction but can change sign within the liquid when they differ. In ten of the thirty-four parameter sets examined, a critical state preferred by the liquid requires a non-ideality favoring mixing. For one such fluid, we construct the coexistence curve, which terminates at the predicted critical point at positive pressure. Attraction and excluded volume provide distinct contributions to the density-order coupling; only the former survives on a fixed lattice with single occupancy. Removing the excluded-volume contribution restores the familiar condition in 58 of the 82 such critical states found. Thus, within this closure, liquid-liquid separation can occur with a non-ideality favoring mixing.

papers.title: Reduced Density Matrices from Renormalization-Group Flows
papers.abstract: We reconstruct complete one- and two-body reduced density matrices (RDMs) by a single collective backward evolution along the in-medium similarity renormalization-group flow. Benchmarks show improved accuracy and physical consistency over conventional elementwise evolution. In neutron matter, two-body RDMs reveal spin-triplet dominance in interaction-dependent Fermi-sea depletion trends. Meanwhile, the forward-backward energy difference provides an internal diagnostic of many-body truncation errors, whose quantification remains challenging in nuclear $ab\ initio$ calculations.

papers.title: An auto-initializing algorithm to determine electronic ground states from random Slater determinants
papers.abstract: Accurate quantum many-body calculations often depend on reliable reference states or good human-designed ans\"atze, yet such knowledge can become unreliable in hard problems like strongly correlated systems. Here we show that high-accuracy many-body ground states can be discovered directly from random Slater determinants. We introduce the Trimmed Configuration Interaction (TrimCI) method, which self-refines by iteratively expanding and trimming configurations in the variational space. TrimCI matches state-of-the-art accuracy using orders of magnitude fewer determinants and computer time: $10^6$-fold fewer than a recent quantum computing calculation on an iron-sulfur cluster, $10^5$-fold fewer than a leading classical method on a larger iron-sulfur cluster in nitrogenase, and over 99% of the ground-state energy of a strongly correlated lattice system from $10^{-28}$ of its Hilbert space, exceeding quantum Monte Carlo accuracy by orders of magnitude in some regimes. TrimCI thus provides an auto-initializing, accurate and highly efficient framework for quantum many-body systems, whose compact explicit wavefunctions enable direct and rapid evaluation of observables.

papers.title: Reframing the coupling force of adaptive resolution simulation in terms of the Liouville-type hierarchy for open systems
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a novel perspective on the coupling force employed to compensate the interface artifacts prevalent in adaptive resolution simulations (AdResS) of open many-particle systems. We show that a substantial part of this "thermodynamic force" can be framed in terms of the theoretical model of the Liouville-type hierarchy for open systems. The correspondence is made explicit for the case of a simple atomistic fluid, for which a one-dimensional integral expression is derived. This enables the analysis for dependencies of the thermodynamic force on important simulation parameters, which is taken to inspire both simplifications for the numerical calculation of the thermodynamic force and new criteria for its validation that are adequate to the interfacial nature of the problem. The theoretical claims are then verified in a simulation study of the atomistic supercritical Lennard-Jones fluid at different thermodynamic states.

papers.title: CRAFT-{\epsilon}: A Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for the Static Relative Permittivity of Pure Organic Liquids
papers.abstract: The static relative permittivity is an important property in thermodynamic modeling, electrochemistry, and solvent design, but predicting it directly from molecular structure remains challenging because both electronic polarization and molecular dipole orientation contribute to the measured response. Here, we introduce CRAFT-{\epsilon} (Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for {\epsilon}), a conformer-resolved molecular descriptor model for predicting the static relative permittivity of neutral pure liquids. Conformer free energies, molecular dipoles, and atom-resolved polarizabilities are obtained from a GFN2-xTB/ALPB 10 workflow. The molecular dipole is decomposed into chemically defined polar-fragment vectors, allowing fitted corrections to retain both the magnitude and relative orientation of local dipolar contributions. Electronic and orientational polarization are combined with a group-contribution molar volume in the Onsager-Kirkwood-Fr\"ohlich relation. A staged parameterization with 41 parameters is applied to nonpolar, polar, and hydrogen-bonding compounds. For 1393 liquids with permittivities between 1.5 and 183, CRAFT-{\epsilon} reaches a five-fold cross-validated average absolute deviation of 2.40 ({R^2} = 0.93). Conformational averaging 15 is essential for liquids with several polar groups. Compared with an established fragment-based model with 139 parameters, it reaches a similar cross-validated RMSE (3.65 versus 3.41) with about a quarter of the parameters and applies to every liquid of the dataset. The resulting framework provides a computationally inexpensive route from molecular structure to liquid dielectric response and forms a basis for later application to solvent mixtures and electrolyte systems.

papers.title: Adiabatic Electronic Momentum and the Continuity Equation with Nonlocal Effective Core Potentials in an Electronic Phase-Space Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: Adiabatic electronic momentum and current density provide fundamental information about electronic motion induced by nuclear motion under the Born-Oppenheimer separation. In practical electronic structure calculations, core electrons in heavy atoms are commonly replaced by effective core potentials (ECPs), whose nonlocal components introduce additional contributions to electronic momentum and the continuity equation. Here, using a phase-space electronic Hamiltonian approach, we investigate these nonlocal components on adiabatic electronic momentum and the continuity equation in small molecules with moving nuclei. We demonstrate that this approach efficiently describes adiabatic electronic momentum and the divergence of electronic current density when the nonlocal contributions to the corresponding electronic operators are properly accounted for. We find that the nonlocal correction to electronic momentum is important when the ECP-centered atoms move but is small otherwise, reflecting the spatial locality of the electronic response and ECP. We further examine the implications of moving ECPs, which account for the motion of nonlocal pseudopotentials with the nuclei to restore Galilean covariance, for adiabatic electronic transport. We show that, for nondegenerate systems with time-reversal symmetry, moving ECPs do not modify the coordinate space adiabatic evolution of time-reversal even observables through second order in nuclear velocity, although they can alter the electronic momentum operator and its feedback on nuclear dynamics.

papers.title: Latent Molecular Rollout Towards Causal World Models: Direction is Learnable, Amplitude Control is Readout-Dependent
papers.abstract: A molecular world model should predict how structural changes alter physical properties, not merely assign labels to static molecules. We build a latent molecular rollout system on an 8B Qwen3 backbone, trained on 9,202 aqueous experimental pKa pairs from iBonD, and assess its progress toward causal control by auditing three often-conflated capabilities: predictive fidelity through the intended molecular pathway, directional learnability versus amplitude calibration of target-conditioned displacements, and transfer of latent control to decoded structures. After removing textual shortcuts, continuous latent inference achieves a test MAE of 2.087, significantly outperforming direct molecular feature readout (MAE difference -0.276, 95% CI [-0.352, -0.203], p<0.001). A target-conditioned policy reliably learns displacement directions, with a median cosine of 0.577 and 62.8% of 43 held-out pairs exceeding the 0.3 threshold. Amplitude conclusions are strictly readout-dependent. A frozen linear readout yields near-zero amplitude correlation (-0.020), while a nonlinear gradient-based readout recovers relative amplitude ordering (correlation 0.585, sign accuracy 0.744-0.767) with compressed absolute scale. At the decoded structure level, neither input-slot editing nor direct final-state injection produces meaningful changes across 80 test sources, bounding the tested control surfaces rather than indicating a universal decoder bottleneck. Generation fine-tuning shows relative improvement under internal oracle evaluation but does not surpass a simple constant baseline in single-sample settings. These results delineate the capability frontier of fixed-scale latent molecular interfaces: directional control is robustly achievable, but calibrated amplitude control and decoded structural transfer remain open challenges on the path to causal molecular world models.

papers.title: Affordable Analytic Gradients for G0W0-BSE Excited States for Multiple GW Variants via Back-Propagation
papers.abstract: We derive, implement and validate analytic nuclear gradients for three variants of $GW$ self-energies---the contour-deformation (CD), the analytic continuation (AC), and the contour deformation with $W$-analytic-continuation (CD-WAC)---and for the Bethe--Salpeter equation (BSE) built on top of them. All gradients are expressed as contractions of a set of covectors connected to derivatives of primitive quantities in SCF calculations. The derivation of these covectors is a back-propagation procedure through the $GW$ and BSE equations. Central finite differences confirm the correctness of all implemented gradients. With the AC-$GW$-BSE gradient we optimize the excited-state geometries of carbon monoxide, a donor-acceptor dye labelled as DA1, and DMABN, a typical model system for twisted intramolecular charge-transfer phenomena (TICT), and have obtained results that successfully reproduce observations from experiments or high-level calculations. We also performed trajectory surface hopping (TSH) simulations of nonadiabatic molecular dynamics (NAMD) of DMABN using the SHARC NAMD package, showing the capacity of our method to simulate NAMD problems. We performed timing and memory scaling tests, demonstrating that the gradient calculations of both $GW$ and BSE scale asymptotically as $N^4$ for timing and $N^3$ for memory. All source codes used in the present work, including the REST program package and the modified SHARC NAMD package that supports REST as the quantum chemistry backend, are available on Gitee https://gitee.com/restgroup/rest and https://gitee.com/qirui-gao-2025/sharc

papers.title: Rovibrational state-specific quasi-classical trajectory calculation and master equation analysis of the CNO system in high-energy collisions
papers.abstract: The CNO system governs the formation and depletion of the CN, CO and NO radiative species relevant to combustion, astrophysical and hypersonic applications. The NO($X^2\Pi$) + C($^3P$), CN($X^2\Sigma^+$) + O($^3P$) and CO($X^1\Sigma^+$) + N($^4S$, $^2D$) collisional systems are investigated using rovibrational state-specific quasi-classical trajectory calculations and master equation analysis under hypersonic thermal conditions. Inelastic processes proceed primarily through rotational excitation of low-lying states and rovibrational excitation of high-lying states. For most systems, rotational and vibrational relaxation times exhibit comparable scales and unconventional temperature dependences, invalidating the assumption of decoupled energy modes. Dissociation is governed by high-lying rovibrational states and correlates strongly with the state-specific energy deficit rather than vibrational-specific dynamics. At $T$ = 10,000 K, 72 to 93% of the depletion of the diatomic species occurs within a quasi-steady-state (QSS) regime for all systems. At lower temperatures, a large portion of the depletion occurs outside the QSS regime, indicating that the QSS assumption holds only for moderate to high temperatures. No such regime is established for exchange reactions, demonstrating that the QSS assumption is invalid for modelling them. The NO + C system proceeds predominantly towards CN + O at low temperatures and towards the CO + N channels at high temperatures, preferentially forming N($^4S$). The fraction proceeding towards the CO + N channels remains lower than in available shock-tube measurements, while the thermal exchange rate coefficients reproduce shock-tube measurements and high-fidelity calculations. Finally, consistent similarities across inelastic, exchange and dissociation processes offer promising physical foundations for reduced-order model development.
